oneliner.t: Registered Democrat from New Jersey with no documented Alaska ties who is serving a 20-year federal prison sentence (D.N.J. No. 3:19-cr-00790) for threatening communications and false bomb threats; a perennial candidate, he placed fourth in the Aug. 18, 2026 primary (3.8%) and reached the November ballot after Democrat Matt Schultz withdrew.

born.note: Year from Wikipedia; consistent with the ages DOJ gave (28 in Oct. 2019, 31 in May 2022, 32 in Dec. 2023). Exact date not published.

hometown.t: Monmouth County (Toms River area), New Jersey

profile.residence: Federal prison in Otisville, NY (filing mailing address: Box Elder, SD)

upbringing.t: Raised in New Jersey; DOJ describes him as formerly of Monmouth County. By his own account (via Wikipedia) he volunteered on political campaigns as a teenager, including Ron Paul's 2012 presidential run, and earlier described himself as an ordained minister and legal consultant; those self-descriptions are not independently documented. From July 2016 to May 2018 he lived outside the United States, the period in which DOJ says he sent the threats. He was arrested in the Northern Mariana Islands in September 2019. His mother, Carol 'Kitty' Hafner, has run for Congress in Alaska and Wyoming; her candidacies are her own record.

platform.t: Medicare for All and free college; opposes Medicaid and food-aid work requirements.
Abolish ICE and legalize all immigrants.
Tax polluters, adopt a Green New Deal and challenge fossil-fuel industries; more environmental rules to stop overfishing.
End aid to Israel and to Ukraine; favors neutrality and opposes foreign military entanglements.
Implement the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples; highlights missing and murdered Indigenous women.
Supports ranked-choice voting; calls state voter-data sharing a privacy violation.

entries.t: Ran as a Republican in Hawaii's 2nd District primary (44.1%, lost).
Ran as a Democrat in Oregon's 3rd District primary (1.4%); his 2018 survey listed legalizing all drugs and 'building socialism' as priorities.

note.t: No documented residence in Alaska. His filing lists a Box Elder, South Dakota mailing address (the same as his mother's) and a New York phone number; he is held at FCI Otisville, NY. AP notes the Constitution requires a House member to be an inhabitant of the state when elected. In 2024 a state judge and the Alaska Supreme Court (4–1) let him stay on the ballot; the Beacon (Sep. 2026) says he could not live in Alaska if elected unless pardoned.

legal.t: Charged by sealed complaint (Oct. 6, 2016) and a 33-count indictment (announced Oct. 31, 2019) in the U.S. District Court for New Jersey, No. 3:19-cr-00790. DOJ says that from July 2016 to May 2018, while abroad, he sent threats to elected officials, judges, police officers, lawyers and their families, tried to extort $350,000, and phoned in false bomb threats to an elected official's office, a county courthouse, a police department, two law firms and a business. On May 17, 2022 he pleaded guilty before Judge Michael A. Shipp to three counts: threatening communications with intent to extort, threatening communications, and conveying false information about an explosive device. On Dec. 7, 2023 Judge Zahid N. Quraishi sentenced him to 240 months (20 years) in prison plus three years of supervised release.
legal.short: Guilty plea: threats, false bomb threats; 20 years
legal.status: Serving sentence (FCI Otisville, NY; BOP projected release Oct. 12, 2036 per AP/Wikipedia). Third Circuit granted summary affirmance Feb. 27, 2026 (No. 26-1120, consol. with 23-3258); rehearing denied May 28, 2026; motion to recall mandate pending as of Jul. 20, 2026. A further appeal (No. 26-1661) was open as of Jul. 27, 2026, flagged for possible dismissal for a jurisdictional defect.

research_notes: Primary Aug. 18, 2026: 6,175 votes (3.8%), fourth of 15; moved into the general after Schultz (3rd) withdrew. Other matters reported only by Wikipedia and not verified here: pre-2019 New Jersey municipal warrants (Middletown, Freehold) on drug and contempt charges, status unknown — charged is not convicted, so not listed under legal; several failed federal suits he filed in forma pauperis in 2023–24 against officials in Maine, Nevada, New Mexico and Vermont over ballot access; his 2024 statement that he expected compassionate release if elected. 2024 ballot fight: Judge Ian Wheeles dismissed the Alaska Democratic Party's suit (Sep. 10, 2024) and the Alaska Supreme Court affirmed 4–1. ADN reported in 2024 that the NRCC appeared to boost him to split the Democratic vote. His mother Carol Hafner's runs (AK House 2018, WY House 2020, AK Senate 2026) are hers, not his. Photo not retrieved (none appropriate).
